findings.certainty: high that these paths publish nil and therefore never republish usage; medium that this is a defect, because the code intentionally treats a countdown retry as an unconfirmable route ('保守地保持未知') and the task explicitly permits showing unknown when the source cannot be confirmed.
findings.evidence: streamWithAutoRetry publishes (nil, revision) on every successful open (Fallback.swift lines 69 and 317). recordContextUsage -> state.recordRequest starts with 'guard let streamEntryID, let streamConfigRevision, …' so a nil streamEntryID is rejected and returns without publishing. beginContextUsageRequest() has already cleared the snapshot at round start, so after a successful transient retry or reminder recovery the indicator stays '—' even though the request succeeded against the current entry and streamResult.turnUsage carries a positive latestContextTokens. The added test testRequestPublicationRejectsUnknownRetryAndUncapturedFallback encodes this nil-entry rejection.

findings.trigger: A turn whose initial stream fails with a retryable error and then succeeds via auto-retry, or a turn recovered by the <system-reminder> round after an empty tool-result response: both call streamWithAutoRetry, which reports the stream-opened signal with a nil entry id.
findings.verification: Drive recordContextUsage (or the fallback/reminder call sites) with a known entry/epoch for the auto-retry and reminder routes at the VM level, or capture device evidence: force a transient error then success (and separately an empty-after-tool-result turn) and confirm whether the indicator updates from '—' or is intended to remain unknown.

findings.certainty: high that no VM-level/integration test exists for the glue layer; medium on product impact because the underlying state-machine invariants that the glue relies on are covered by the existing tests.
findings.evidence: The added tests exercise ContextUsageState/ContextUsageSnapshot/ContextUsageIdentity and recordRequest in isolation (record/snapshot/invalidate, matchesRoute, nil streamEntryId, config-revision change, fallback epoch, late result). No test instantiates AIChatViewModel, calls recordContextUsage/captureContextUsageIdentities, or asserts the retry/reminder/fallback call sites, so the acceptance-critical integration between ProviderConfigStore.configRevision, resolveCurrentEntry and the state machine remains unproven by automated evidence.

findings.verification: Add VM-level or integration unit tests around recordContextUsage covering: same-entry config-revision change rejected, pre-captured group member fallback accepted with the new epoch, resolveCurrentEntry returning a different entry rejected, and an older requestRevision rejected after invalidate/beginContextUsageRequest; or record equivalent device evidence.

limitations: Read-only static review: nothing was built, installed or run, so the task-record claim of a successful Xcode build and of '9 pure-logic tests passed' could not be reproduced, and no runtime/device behavior was observed. All unexecuted tests: the whole MinisTests suite (ContextUsageTests 15 methods, ContextPolicyTests, ThinkingLevelTests, etc.) and any Xcode build. The ContextUsageIndicator UI (position left of mic, fixed reserved width, ring glyph/percentage spacing, ViewThatFits compact fallback of the read-aloud/edit-exit labels, Dynamic Type scaling, light/dark, VoiceOver value/hint, 44x34pt tap area vs accidental mic/send/focus taps, keyboard open/close, voice and history-edit states) is unverified statically; the '—' empty-ring layout and the per-value spacing the user deferred to code need on-device evidence. Task acceptance evidence lives in validation.md, 实施进展 and the other task-listed norms (plan-task, resume-task, docs/harness/record-formats.md, operations.md, ios-ui-design Apple reference) which are not in the required-Spec set and were not taken as binding, so per-item acceptance could not be cross-checked. The VM glue (captureContextUsageIdentities + recordContextUsage + resolveCurrentEntry wiring, and the retry/<system-reminder> streamWithAutoRetry routes) has no dedicated automated test; only the pure ContextUsageState machine is tested, so the R1 behavior below rests on code reading. recordContextUsage is only reached after a stream completes, so canceled/interrupted turns were not traced end-to-end. Excluded deps/ish and deps/proot were not needed. No findings is not proof of runtime correctness, and this report is review input, not a final product-acceptance decision.
